learningObjectives: Explain what the Tricentis Mobile Agent provides and what setup burden it removes.
Prepare an Android device for test automation.
Scan a mobile application and distinguish native/hybrid opening from mobile website opening, including Desired Capabilities setup.
Configure a remote TMA using documented server formats, distinguishing REST binding from the Appium port.
Diagnose mobile setup failures by separating device-side problems from Tosca-side ones.

elements.description: Mobile automation traditionally means assembling a toolchain — Appium, Java components, environment variables, device drivers — before a single test can run. The Tricentis Mobile Agent (TMA) provides simplified setup and configuration of iOS and Android devices so that none of that is your problem: you do not need to install Appium, Java components, or configure environment variables yourself.

Mobile Engine 3.0 steers supported mobile applications through a configured connection. Modules use the familiar Tosca TestCase workflow, but application type, supported controls, capabilities and device preparation still affect execution.

bulletPoints: TMA = the setup layer. Mobile Engine 3.0 = the steering layer.
No manual Appium / Java / environment-variable configuration required.

elements.description: Local (TMA) uses a locally connected supported device or Android emulator. Select a device explicitly when required by the topology; a single local Android device does not require DeviceName. Check the requirements for the installed Agent version.
Remote (TMA) reaches an Agent on another machine and its supported device, emulator or simulator. Remote TMA is distinct from connecting directly to a cloud provider’s Appium endpoint.

elements.text: The authoring model stays the same, but moving a test requires validating device/app compatibility, capabilities and connection configuration. TMA 2025.4 requirements restrict iOS hosting to macOS; older Agent/Tosca guides describe broader host support. Use the installed Agent version’s requirements rather than assuming those descriptions apply unchanged.

bulletPoints: Local and remote describe connection topology, not separate TestCase languages.
Validate host/device support against the installed TMA version; newer and legacy guides differ.

elements.title: Android prerequisites
items: On the device, allow access to phone data when prompted.
Enable USB debugging: Settings → Developer options → USB debugging.
Ensure the USB driver for that device is installed on the computer.

elements.text: If Windows recognizes a phone but automation cannot reach it, check USB debugging, authorization, data access and the device driver. Recognition alone does not prove automation readiness; missing debugging is one possible cause, not a proven most-common diagnosis.

bulletPoints: Allow data access · enable USB debugging · install the USB driver.

elements.description: The Mobile Scan handles native, hybrid, and web applications on mobile. The sequence is: prepare the test environment, start the Mobile Scan and connect to your device, then add the mobile device, emulator, or simulator you want to scan against. From there, scanning produces Modules the same way it does for any other technology.

The connection to a device, emulator, or simulator is established through test configuration parameters. This is the same TCP mechanism used elsewhere in Tosca — for the TestDataService endpoint, for SelfHealing — so the scoping rules you already know apply.

Use Open Mobile App for native/hybrid applications before steering them. The Standard Mobile Module reference documents an exception: Set Desired Capabilities may precede it. Mobile websites instead start with OpenUrl, Browser=ChromeAndroid or SafariiOS, and UseActiveTab left empty.

elements.text: Opening rules depend on the resource and setup Modules. Do not generalize an unconditional first-step rule across Excel file comparison, mobile web and native applications.

elements.title: Examples from Standard modules → Engines → Mobile (platform support varies)
items: Open Mobile App — native/hybrid opening, after any required Desired Capabilities setup. Switch Mobile App switches applications.
Set Desired Capabilities — configures the Appium capabilities for the session.
Click On Screen · Swipe On Screen · Draw On Screen — coordinate-based gestures for when no control is addressable.
Send Text Input To Focused Control · Set Autohide Keyboard — text entry and keyboard behaviour.
ME3.0 Hardware Button Operations · ME3.0 Set Device Orientation — physical buttons and rotating the device.
Upload File to Mobile Device · Download File from Mobile Device — Android file transfer.
Get Appium Session Id · End Appium Session — session lifecycle control.
Android Snackbar — steers the Android transient message component.
Biometrics: Use Android fingerprint authentication · Use iOS biometric authentication · Set iOS biometrics enrollment (iOS simulator). Check each Module’s supported environment.

elements.text: 📄 Official Tricentis Academy exercise material for this lesson is not redistributed here — complete the exercises inside the official course. This lesson requires a physical device, emulator, or simulator, so check that prerequisite first.

bulletPoints: Mobile automation covers native, hybrid and web applications with different opening paths.
TCPs and Desired Capabilities configure the connection and session.
Open Mobile App opens native/hybrid apps; OpenUrl opens mobile websites.

elements.description: The Tosca mobile configuration guide gives remote addresses as http://<ip_address>:<port_number>/. Keep the documented trailing slash. It does not establish that every missing-slash failure has one exact error or that the Scan wizard always tolerates it.

elements.term: REST binding is not the Appium port
elements.description: The TMA 2025.4 CLI binds services to localhost by default. Use --rest-address <IP>:<port> for a reachable web-server binding. --appium-port configures Appium separately; --grpc-address configures gRPC. Match the service endpoint required by Tosca rather than treating these switches as interchangeable.

elements.term: Diagnose one layer at a time
elements.description: Check Agent/device availability, the endpoint from the Tosca host, session logs, capabilities and application identifiers. A connected or idle device status alone cannot rule out firewall, routing, permissions or session-creation problems. No undocumented REST response schema is required for this lesson.

elements.title: Specify an installed Android application
items: Obtain the package and launch activity from the application team or a verified Android tool for that build.
Enter them in AppPackage and AppActivity. This method requires the app to be installed.
Alternatively, Application Path points to an APK that Tosca installs. BundleID identifies an iOS app; it is not an Android APK installation field.

elements.description: TMA 2025.4 documents bare-metal hosts and requires the Android emulator to run on the same machine as the Agent. It supports Android Studio for Android virtual devices and Xcode for iOS virtual devices. Confirm host architecture, OS and emulator support for your installed versions before setup.

elements.text: Do not diagnose every APK parsing failure as a v1-signature problem or blindly re-sign the app: changing signing identity can affect updates and behavior. Obtain a compatible test build from its owner and inspect the actual installation error.

Device vendor policies and Android settings vary. The public preparation guide documents USB debugging, phone data access and drivers, not a universal instruction to disable protections or skip every permission-related requirement.

bulletPoints: Use the documented address format with its trailing slash.
REST, Appium and gRPC are separate service bindings.
A device status check is evidence for one layer, not proof that all connectivity is healthy.
Check the installed Agent’s host/OS requirements; place the emulator with the Agent.

examPitfalls.title: Applying one opening rule to every mobile test
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using Open Mobile App for websites or ignoring required capability setup.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Open Mobile App for native/hybrid applications before steering them. The Standard Mobile Module reference documents an exception: Set Desired Capabilities may precede it. Mobile websites instead start with OpenUrl, Browser=ChromeAndroid or SafariiOS, and UseActiveTab left empty.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Appium must be installed and configured manually
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Setting up Appium, Java components, and environment variables before starting mobile automation in Tosca.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Tricentis Mobile Agent exists precisely to remove that work — it provides simplified setup and configuration of iOS and Android devices without requiring you to install Appium or Java components or configure environment variables.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting to enable USB debugging on the Android device
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Connecting the phone by USB, seeing it recognised by Windows, and concluding the device is ready.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The device must have USB debugging enabled under Settings → Developer options, must allow access to phone data, and the USB driver must be installed on the computer. Without USB debugging the Mobile Agent cannot reach the device.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking Remote (TMA) requires different TestCases
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Rebuilding TestCases when moving from a locally attached device to a remote device farm.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Local and remote use the same authoring model. Validate capabilities, app and platform compatibility as well as connection configuration when moving a test.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Mobile Scan only handles native apps
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reaching for the XBrowser Engine to test a web application running in a mobile browser.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Mobile Scan supports native, hybrid, and web applications on mobile. Scanning a mobile web app through the Mobile Scan gives you the device context that a desktop browser scan cannot.

examPitfalls.title: Omitting the trailing slash from the TMAServer TCP
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using an address inconsistent with the documented remote endpoint format, then assuming a successful scan proves execution connectivity.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented http://<ip_address>:<port_number>/ format. Validate scan and execution configuration separately; neither a successful scan nor a generic error proves one particular root cause.

examPitfalls.title: Starting a remote Mobile Agent from the tray icon
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Launching TMA normally on a second machine, seeing its console load in the browser from the Tosca machine, and assuming remote connection is fully enabled.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The TMA 2025.4 CLI binds services to localhost by default. Use --rest-address <IP>:<port> for a reachable web-server binding. --appium-port configures Appium separately; --grpc-address configures gRPC. Match the service endpoint required by Tosca rather than treating these switches as interchangeable.

examPitfalls.title: Ignoring the installed Agent’s support matrix
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming an older Windows/iOS or emulator guide applies to every later Agent build.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TMA 2025.4 documents bare-metal hosts and requires the Android emulator to run on the same machine as the Agent. It supports Android Studio for Android virtual devices and Xcode for iOS virtual devices. Confirm host architecture, OS and emulator support for your installed versions before setup. TMA 2025.4 lists iOS hosts as macOS only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For a native/hybrid mobile TestCase that does not set Desired Capabilities first, which Module opens the app before steering?

options.text: Connect to Mobile Agent
Open Mobile App
Mobile Scan
Any Module — the order is unconstrained.

practiceQuiz.hint: Choose the native/hybrid opening Module; mobile websites use a different path.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Open Mobile App opens native/hybrid applications. Desired Capabilities setup is the documented exception to first position. Mobile websites use OpenUrl.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the documented native/hybrid opening Module. Connection parameters establish the device connection.
optionExplanations.B: Open Mobile App is the native/hybrid opening Module in this scenario. Capability setup may precede it when needed.
optionExplanations.C: Mobile Scan creates Modules during authoring; it is not the runtime opening TestStep.
optionExplanations.D: Opening must precede app steering; the order is not unconstrained.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the Tricentis Mobile Agent remove the need to do?

options.text: Writing TestCases — TMA generates them automatically.
Installing Appium and Java components, and configuring environment variables.
Enabling USB debugging on the device.
Scanning the mobile application.

practiceQuiz.hint: It removes toolchain setup, not device setup or test authoring.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA provides simplified setup and configuration of iOS and Android devices so you do not need to install Appium or Java components or configure environment variables. Device-side steps like USB debugging, and the scanning and authoring work, still apply.

optionExplanations.A: TMA manages connectivity and setup, not automatic creation of the intended TestCases.
optionExplanations.B: TMA packages the Appium/Java setup so those components and environment variables do not need manual assembly.
optionExplanations.C: Android device preparation, including USB debugging, still applies.
optionExplanations.D: Scanning and authoring remain part of the mobile testing workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Android phone is visible in Windows, but automation cannot reach it. USB debugging is confirmed disabled. Which prerequisite should be corrected?

options.text: USB debugging has not been enabled under Settings → Developer options.
The phone needs a Tosca licence.
Only iOS devices are supported.
Remote (TMA) must be used for all physical devices.

practiceQuiz.hint: Windows recognising the device is not the same as the device permitting automation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Android preparation requires allowing access to phone data, enabling USB debugging under Settings → Developer options, and having the USB driver installed. A device can charge and be recognised by Windows while still refusing debugging access.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario explicitly confirms this required Android setting is disabled; enabling and authorizing debugging addresses that prerequisite.
optionExplanations.B: The documented device preparation issue is debugging access, not installing a Tosca license on the phone.
optionExplanations.C: Android is a supported mobile platform; this is not an iOS-only tool.
optionExplanations.D: Physical Android devices can use local connections; Remote TMA is a topology choice.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the difference between Local (TMA) and Remote (TMA)?

options.text: Local supports Android only; Remote supports iOS only.
Local connects a device, emulator or simulator to the workstation running Tosca; Remote uses a remotely installed Mobile Agent to reach a remote device.
Local is for scanning, Remote is for execution.
Remote TestCases must be written differently from Local ones.

practiceQuiz.hint: The distinction is where the agent and the device live, not what they support.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Local and remote describe where the Agent/device connection resides. The authoring model stays the same; capabilities, app compatibility and the installed Agent support matrix must still be validated.

optionExplanations.A: Local/remote is not an Android-versus-iOS split. Support depends on the installed Agent/platform versions.
optionExplanations.B: This distinguishes a local device connection from an Agent/device on a remote host.
optionExplanations.C: Both connection types can support scanning and execution; those are separate workflow stages.
optionExplanations.D: The authoring model is shared. Validate configuration and compatibility rather than inventing a different TestCase language.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which application types can the Mobile Scan handle?

options.text: Native applications only.
Native and hybrid applications only.
Native, hybrid, and web applications.
Web applications only — native apps require a custom control.

practiceQuiz.hint: It covers the full range of what runs on a phone.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Mobile Scan supports scanning native, hybrid, and web applications, after the test environment has been prepared and the device, emulator or simulator has been connected.

optionExplanations.A: Native apps are only one supported application type.
optionExplanations.B: This excludes supported mobile web applications.
optionExplanations.C: Mobile automation covers native, hybrid and web apps, with different preparation and opening paths.
optionExplanations.D: Native apps are supported without a universal custom-control requirement.

quickRecap.value: Simplified iOS/Android setup — no manual Appium, Java components, or environment variables.
Device via USB, or simulator/emulator, on the Tosca workstation.
Remotely installed agent connecting to a remote device/emulator/simulator.
Allow phone data access · Settings → Developer options → USB debugging · USB driver installed.
Handles native, hybrid, and web mobile applications; prepare environment → start scan → connect device.
Native/hybrid opening before steering; Set Desired Capabilities is an exception. Mobile websites use OpenUrl.
Use the documented remote http://<ip_address>:<port_number>/ format. Do not infer an exact error or universal scan behavior.
--rest-address binds the web server; --appium-port configures Appium separately. Defaults bind locally.
Check devices, endpoints, logs and session setup separately; a connected/idle status cannot prove complete connectivity.
AppPackage/AppActivity identify an installed Android app; Application Path installs a build. BundleID identifies an iOS app.
Android emulator and Agent share a host; use the installed version’s supported hardware and OS matrix.
Vendor policies vary. Diagnose permission/signing failures and obtain an approved compatible test build instead of assuming one bypass fixes all failures.
